svg.title: Signed ToF offsets in the driver camera frame
svg.desc: A not-to-scale side view. Positive camera-forward distance points from the driver camera to the face. Sensor Z is positive when the sensor is ahead of the camera. Eye correction is positive if the eye plane is farther than the returned surface and negative if closer. The hypothetical example is 48 centimetres raw plus 1 bias plus 0.5 sensor offset minus 0.5 eye correction, giving 49 centimetres eye depth. These are not assumed forehead settings.

g.text: ToF offsets: measure the sign as well as the size
Side-view sketch — NOT to scale. Numbers are an example, not your settings.
s = the driver camera's forward axis (+Z in the CAMERA frame).
It is not the LCD world's vertical Z. Positive s points from the camera toward the face.
+s toward face
Driver
camera
ToF
Eye plane
Returned
surface
Corrected surface range = raw 48 + bias 1 = 49 cm
Sensor Z offset = +0.5 cm (sensor ahead of camera)
Eye-plane correction = −0.5 cm (eye plane closer here)
Camera-to-eye depth = 49 cm
Eye depth = raw + bias + sensor Z + eye correction
Your face may give the OPPOSITE eye-correction sign. Measure it; do not copy this example.
Sensor behind the camera? Sensor Z is negative. Eye plane farther than surface? Correction is positive.
A forehead, glasses, hand or background may return the pulse. Range does not identify pupils.
Finish the range fit, then check real eye depth independently on the final fixed mount.
